## Learning goals

**I will be able to** identify parallel branches and calculate equivalent resistance, source current, branch current, and power.

**This is useful because I can** explain how several loads operate independently from one source.

**Used in university:** Circuit analysis, electrical distribution, instrumentation, electronics, and computer hardware.

## Common voltage

Components are in parallel when both ends connect to the same two nodes. Every branch has the same voltage:

$$
V_k = V_T
$$

## General parallel rules

The source current is the sum of the branch currents:

$$
I_T = \sum_{k=1}^{n} I_k
$$

The equivalent resistance is

$$
\frac{1}{R_T} = \sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{R_k}
$$

For exactly two parallel resistors, the product-over-sum shortcut is

$$
R_T = \frac{R_aR_b}{R_a+R_b}
$$

Calculate any branch current with Ohm's law:

$$
I_k = \frac{V_T}{R_k}
$$

Total power equals the sum of the branch powers:

$$
P_T = \sum_{k=1}^{n}P_k = V_T I_T
$$

## Check the answer

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n} I_k \overset{?}{=} I_T
$$

The equivalent resistance must be smaller than the smallest branch resistance.
